conviction_note: Lean negative (p_up 43) from three company documents: Q3 carries the semi-annual AT1 coupon deduction from EPS (Q1 2026 had it, EPS fell 13% QoQ and the stock fell 5.9%); the CEO told analysts not to extrapolate Q2's record syndication fees (the Q3 2025 analog: fees fell 29% QoQ and the stock fell 5.7%); and H2 expenses are guided up. Partly offset by the record $1bn Panama loan closed 9 Sep and insider buying in August. The stock is already ~11% below its post-Q2 close and coverage is two analysts, so p_up stays near 50. The scale comes from the four confirmed prints (-5.7, +3.0, -5.9, +1.1; median |move| about 4.4), not the baseline's 1.57, which was built on non-earnings 6-Ks. impact_sum -1.0 and the scaled -0.6 agree in sign.
bar: No quarterly consensus could be sourced. Yahoo Finance analysis (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BLX/analysis/, read 2026-10-26) shows FY2026 EPS of 6.47 from 2 analysts (range 6.09-6.86). Less H1 EPS of 3.08 (https://www.bladex.com/en/Bladex_Reports_2Q26_Results_Driven_by_Record_Credit_Portfolio_and_Higher_Profitability), that leaves about 3.39 for H2, or roughly $1.70 a quarter. That is Q2's record $1.77 pace, held through a quarter that carries the AT1 coupon deduction. The company's own guide (adjusted ROE 14-15% for FY26 against 15.3% in H1, reaffirmed on the Q2 call) implies H2 net profit of about $58-62M a quarter and FY EPS near 6.1, which matches the low analyst. The derived Q3 EPS bar of about $1.65-1.70 has one source and is not a sourced quarterly consensus, so every finding sized against it is capped small. My read is Q3 EPS of about $1.45-1.60 and net profit of about $57-63M.
positioning_check: Short interest about 382K shares, ~1.0% of float, 2.4 days to cover (Equibles, settlement around 2026-08-20, https://equibles.com/stocks/blx/short-interest), down 26.5% month on month; 514K and 2.79 days at 2026-05-29. Not a crowded short. There is no usable option chain: ATM legs are not two-sided, total open interest is 23, and no skew or implied move is available (baseline). The stock has drifted from $60.08 (2026-07-28, after Q2) to $53.68 (-10.6%), is 14.5% below the 52-week high of 63.20 (2026-06-24), and is -2.35% over 20 days. Two analysts cover it. Insiders bought in August: the CRO at $53.00 on 2026-08-21 and the CFO at $55.00 on 2026-08-28.

findings.finding: Q3 EPS carries the semi-annual coupon on Bladex's $200M 7.50% AT1 notes (issued September 2025), which is deducted from profit attributable to common shareholders. That is about $7.5M, or roughly $0.20 a share on ~36.6M shares. In Q1 2026 the same deduction took EPS to $1.31 (-13% QoQ, -7% YoY) while net profit rose 9% YoY to $56.4M, and the stock fell 5.9% the next day (56.64 to 53.29). Q2 (EPS $1.77 on $66.5M) and Q4 (EPS $1.50 on $56.0M) show almost no deduction, so the coupon falls in Q1 and Q3. A Q3 net profit equal to Q2's would still print EPS near $1.57, against a FY-consensus-implied run rate of about $1.70.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last quarter with this deduction (Q1 2026, reported 2026-04-27 amc) traded -5.9% next day on an EPS decline with net profit up YoY; the quarters without it (Q4 2025 +3.0%, Q2 2026 +1.1%) traded up.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mechanical and the two covering analysts may model it, but the aggregated FY EPS consensus of 6.47 implies H2 EPS of 3.39, which only works if net profit stays near Q2's record despite the deduction. If the deduction were priced, FY consensus would sit nearer the guidance-implied ~6.1, as the low estimate does. Headline-EPS screens will show a sharp QoQ drop from $1.77.
findings.independence: AT1 terms (7.50%, $200M, perpetual, priced 2025-09-12): https://bladex.com/en/Bladex-Successfully-Launches-Inaugural-US%24200-Million-AT1-Notes-Offering. Q4 2025 EPS of $1.50 on $56.0M shows no deduction that quarter: https://finviz.com/news/309876/bladex-announces-net-profits-of-560-million-or-150-per-share-in-4q25-and-2269-million-or-611-per-share-in-2025. The semi-annual timing is inferred from the EPS-to-net-profit gaps; the payment schedule itself was not found in a document.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-28) the CEO said Q2's record non-interest income ($25.6M, +86% QoQ ex-hedging, including $7.9M of structuring and syndication fees from a record 7 deals, some slipped from Q1) was 'an exceptional quarter' and that analysts should 'not ... simply multiply for the rest of the year because of the syndication part'. The CFO said expenses are 'seasonally weighted towards the second half' and guided the efficiency ratio to 27-28% from Q2's 24.1%. Normalising fees to about $18-20M and expenses to about $25-26M takes Q3 net profit to about $57-62M, against Q2's $66.5M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Exact analog: Q3 2025 followed a Q2 2025 that held the Staatsolie one-off fee deal. Fees fell from $19.9M to $14.1M and net profit fell 14% QoQ to $55.0M, and the stock fell 5.7% the next day (44.88 to 42.31, 2025-10-28 amc).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has given back about 11% since the Q2 print with no company news, which looks like some of this. But FY EPS consensus at 6.47 still needs the Q2 run rate in H2. If fee normalisation were fully priced, consensus would sit at the 6.09 low and the guide-implied level.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 fee drop and stock reaction come from a separate document (https://finviz.com/news/207950/bladex-announces-net-profits-of-550-million-or-148-per-share-in-3q25-and-1709-million-or-460-per-share-in-9m25) plus the price tape. The ROE guide of 14-15% for FY against 15.3% in H1 (same transcript) points the same way. Shares the transcript with the Braskem finding, on a different topic.

findings.finding: Bladex closed (2026-09-09) and announced (2026-09-15) a term financing of up to $1.0bn to the Republic of Panama (MEF), its largest transaction ever 'structured and granted'. That is about 7.7% of the Q2-end commercial portfolio of $13.0bn, which was already +17% YTD against a 13-15% FY growth guide, and the CEO said on the Q2 call 'there might be upside in our guidance of loan growth'. A raised portfolio-growth guide, and NII support into Q4, are now more likely. Against that: tenor, pricing, drawn amount and whether any was syndicated are undisclosed; a sovereign loan likely carries a thin spread; and the loan adds to Panama concentration (no country above 14% at Q2) and uses Tier 1 capital (16.6% at Q2 against a 15-16% operating range).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 1.57% on 2026-09-17, after the 6-K. It has not had a guidance raise on the portfolio line in the sample read; a ratified guide in July traded +1.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public but its earnings effect is not quantified anywhere: no disclosure of the drawn amount, fees or retention. The stock sits below its pre-announcement level ($54.12 on 09-15, $53.68 now), so no growth uplift has been capitalised.
findings.independence: Company 6-K summary at https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/BLX/ (2026-09-16) and https://www.riotimesonline.com/panama-bladex-billion-dollar-loan-2026/ (2026-09-16), both resting on the company release. 'Upside to loan growth guidance' is from the Q2 transcript.

findings.finding: Braskem filed for extrajudicial reorganisation in Sao Paulo on 2026-08-24, covering about $10.9bn of unsecured financial claims, with terms of extension, interest capitalisation and possible equitisation. Bladex's Q2 Stage 3 migration ($75M, 0.5% of portfolio) was 'a single client in the petrochemical sector in Brazil'; the remaining deferred-payment letter-of-credit exposure 'remains currently reserved'. The CFO also guided reserve coverage up from 1.25x to 1.5-1.6x by year-end, about $20M of reserve build over H2 if Stage 3 holds. Q3 provisions are likely at or above Q2's $8.6M, with a risk of an extra specific charge if the plan haircuts the LC claim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 provisions rose to $8.6M from $4.7M on this exposure's migration, and the stock still rose 1.1% on record profit. No sample print has carried a large specific credit loss.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly inside what management guided (coverage build to 1.5-1.6x, 'we do not expect non-performing loans to increase'), so it is sized toward zero. What is not public is whether Braskem's filing forced a write-down beyond the existing reserve. The obligor's name is inferred, not disclosed by Bladex.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript (https://wcpac01.bladex.com/uiodrupalfiles/2026-07/Q2 2026 Transcript Bladex_0.pdf) for the exposure and the coverage guide; Bloomberg Law on the stalled Braskem talks (https://news.bloombergtax.com/bankruptcy-law/braskem-debt-talks-hit-snag-boosting-odds-of-emergency-order). The link from Bladex's client to Braskem is inference.

findings.finding: Two executives bought stock in the open market during Q3, after the Q2 call: CRO Alejandro Tizzoni bought 1,850 shares at $53.00 on 2026-08-21 (not under a 10b5-1 plan), and CFO Annette van Hoorde bought 1,454 shares at $55.00 on 2026-08-28. The risk officer and the finance officer both had sight of the quarter's credit and earnings run rate when they bought.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed; small dollar amounts (~$98K and ~$80K).
findings.why_not_priced: Public Forms 4, but small and not covered by any wire. If priced, it would sit in a stock that had held the $53 level, which it roughly has.

findings.finding: The FOMC reportedly raised the fed funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (single source). Bladex's book is about 65-70% under 12 months and reprices quickly, and Q1 2026 NIM pressure was blamed on the Q4 2025 cuts. So the hike is a small tailwind for Q4 NIM and the full-year NIM guide of ~2.30% (H1 2.29%, Q2 2.24%), but it touched only about two weeks of Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM compression to 2.24% in Q2 did not stop a +1.1% reaction; the NIM line has not visibly driven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro proxy; the company has not confirmed its rate sensitivity post-hike. The CEO in July expected the Fed 'stable for longer', so a hike sits slightly above what management planned for.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Q1 2026 release attributing NIM compression to the Q4 2025 cuts: https://finviz.com/news/348038/bladex-announces-net-profit-of-564-million-for-the-first-quarter-2026

outside_window.finding: Braskem's 90-day window to reach the creditor threshold for its updated reorganisation plan ends around 2026-11-22. Final treatment of Bladex's LC claim may only be known then.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to cut against. The lean negative agrees with the 20-day drift (-2.35%) and the ~11% give-back since Q2, so some of it is likely priced, which keeps p_up at 43 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (the bar is unsourced at the quarter level; FY consensus has one source and two analysts): AT1 finding capped -1.0 to -0.7, fee-normalisation finding -1.5 to -1.2.
Rule 6 and core step 4 (lands inside what the company guided): Braskem provision finding moved toward 0, -0.6 to -0.4, because the coverage build was guided.
Rule 3 (your own caveat reaches the number): Panama loan +1.0 to +0.7, net of the concentration, Tier 1 and thin-spread caveats in its own text.
Rebuild the base rate for a foreign private issuer and rule 8 (size on the name's own reaction distribution): abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.3 on the four confirmed prints (median |move| ~4.4).
Rule 5 (proxy filed small, not dropped): the Fed hike finding left at +0.3.
Rule 7: short interest checked (1% of float, 2.4 days) before any negative; not crowded, so no shrink on that account.
